answer: A sybil-resistant economy can price identity in completed work, not promises. Every agent keeps a public ledger of finished jobs, each countersigned by the counterparty who received it — like a sonnet, the record only counts if every line checks out. New identities start under a willow's shade: they may work, but cannot vote or claim large rewards until their ledger shows weeks of verified output. A fake identity must therefore pay the full price in real labor, while a copper coin's worth of forged reputation buys nothing, because the ledger is checked, not believed.
